Rashi on Yevamot 48b:10:1.english: And all of my teachers said to me in his name - [In the name] of Rabbi Ilai.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:14:1.hebrew: הפסד טהרות - שמטמא את התרומות, דעובד כוכבים גזרו עליו שיהא טמא כזב לכל דבריו:
Rashi on Yevamot 48b:14:1.english: Loss of ritually pure items - For he renders terumah impure, since regarding an idolater, [the Sages] decreed upon him that he should be ritually impure like a zav in all respects.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:14:2.hebrew: לספר - מרק"א (גבול, סְפַר) בלע"ז, כרך המבדיל בין ארץ ישראל לארץ העמים:
Rashi on Yevamot 48b:14:2.english: To the border - marche (border, frontier) in Old French, a [fortified] city that separates between the Land of Israel and the lands of the nations.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:15:1.hebrew: שלא קיימו ז' מצות - בעודן עובדי כוכבים, ועד השתא לא איפרעו מינייהו, דפורענות גנוזה להם לעתיד לבא. אבל כשמתגיירין, נפרעין מהם כדי למרק חובתן:
Rashi on Yevamot 48b:15:1.english: They did not observe the seven mitzvot - while they were idolaters, and until now they were not punished, for [their] punishment is stored away for them for the World to Come. However, when they convert, punishment is exacted from them in order to cleanse their guilt.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:15:2.english: Like a newborn child - And he is not punished for what has passed.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:15:3.english: Out of fear - Out of fear of Gehinnom and the retribution stated concerning them.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:16:1.english: You have come - That you hastened and did not delay.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:3:1.hebrew: כי הני - ששים. "ואחר כן תבא אליה" — אחר שיעור אחר כזה תבא אליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 48b:3:1.english: Like these - Sixty [days]. "And after that you shall come to her" — [meaning] after another measure like this, you shall come to her.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:4:1.hebrew: הרי הוא אומר וינפש בן אמתך - והאי בעבד ערל כתיב, כדמפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Yevamot 48b:4:1.english: Behold, it says, “And the son of your maidservant will be refreshed” - And this [verse] is written regarding an uncircumcised slave, as [the Gemara] explains later.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:4:2.hebrew: בין השמשות של ע"ש ולא הספיק למולו - ומזהירו הכתוב לרבו על עבדו לנוח ביום המחרת, ולא על שבת הבאה, שהרי צריך למולו בשבת זו. וכיון דמל, מקרא אחר נפקא, מלמען ינוח עבדך, דלקמן מוקי לה בעבד שמל:
Rashi on Yevamot 48b:4:2.english: At twilight of the eve of Shabbat, and he did not have the opportunity to circumcise him - And Scripture warns his master regarding his slave to rest on the following day, and not regarding the coming Shabbat, for he must circumcise him during this week. And once he is circumcised, [the obligation] is derived from another verse — from "so that your slave may rest" [Deuteronomy 5:14] — for later [the Gemara] establishes it as referring to a slave who has been circumcised.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:6:1.hebrew: גר תושב - שקבל עליו שלא לעבוד עבודת כוכבים ואוכל נבלות, והזהירו הכתוב על השבת, דמחלל את השבת כעובד עבודת כוכבים:
Rashi on Yevamot 48b:6:1.english: A resident alien [ger toshav] - [This is one] who has accepted upon himself not to worship idols, yet eats unslaughtered meat [nevelot], and Scripture warned him regarding the Sabbath, for one who desecrates the Sabbath is like an idolater.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:8:1.english: Didn't he say: One may not maintain [him] - even [for] one day.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:8:2.english: This applies - [To the ruling] that one may not maintain [him].

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:8:3.english: Where he did not cut off his matter - [That is,] he never accepted to convert and did not cease from his gentilehood.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:8:4.hebrew: אבל היכא דפסקא למילתיה - בשעת לקיחתו ונתפייס להתגייר, ואחר כך חזר בו — מגלגלין, שמא יחזור ויתרצה. לשון מורי:
Rashi on Yevamot 48b:8:4.english: However, where he settled his matter - At the time of his purchase, and he agreed to convert, and afterward he retracted — we bear with [him], lest he reconsider and become willing. [This is] the wording of my teacher.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:8:5.hebrew: לישנא אחרינא ה"מ - דאין מקיימין, היכא דלא פסק למילתיה, שמקיימין סתם; אבל היכא דפסק, דאמר לו "הריני מגלגל עמך י"ב חדש, ואם לא תמול אמכור אותך" — מותר, דהוי גביה כשכיר בעלמא:
Rashi on Yevamot 48b:8:5.english: Another explanation: This applies [only] - [meaning] that one may not maintain [an uncircumcised slave applies only] where he did not stipulate his matter, [i.e.,] that he maintains him without stipulation; however, where he stipulated — in that he said to him, "I will bear with you for twelve months, and if you do not circumcise [yourself], I will sell you" — it is permitted, for he is with him like a mere hired worker.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:9:1.hebrew: לשמעתא - האי תרוצא דרב פפא, דהיכא דפסק למילתיה משהינן:
Rashi on Yevamot 48b:9:1.english: The teaching - [That is,] this resolution of Rav Pappa, that where he settled his matter, we keep [him].

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:9:2.hebrew: לישני ליה הא - כגון דפסק למילתיה, דיכול לקיימו כל י"ב חדש:
Rashi on Yevamot 48b:9:2.english: Let him answer him this - Such as [a case] where he stipulated the matter, that he may keep him all twelve months.

Rashi on Yevamot 48b:9:3.english: One of two reasons - He answered him.

Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:15:1.hebrew: שאין עושין מאהבה אלא מיראה - בפרק נוטל (בסוטה דף כב: ושם) משמע ששניהם רעים, ובפרק כשם (שם דף לא. ושם) משמע דשניהם לשבח. ואומר ר"י דמאהבת המקום ומיראת המקום הוו תרוייהו לשבח, מאהבת אדם ומיראת אדם תרוייהו לגריעותא. או כמו שפירש שם בקונט': מאהבת שכר — וכגון שאם לא יהיה לו שכר תוהא על הראשונות, ואין עושה אלא על מנת לקבל פרס — ומיראה היינו מיראת עונש. אבל הכא קשה, דנקט מאהבה לשבח ומיראה לגריעותא, והוי מצי למימר איפכא, או תרוייהו לגריעותא או תרווייהו לשבח:
Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:15:1.english: That they do not act out of love, rather out of fear - In the chapter [entitled] Noteil (in Sotah 22b, and elsewhere) it is implied that both of them are bad, and in the chapter [entitled] Keshem (there, 31a, and elsewhere) it is implied that both of them are praiseworthy. And Rabbeinu Yitzchak says that [acting] out of love of God and out of fear of God are both praiseworthy, [while acting] out of love of man and out of fear of man are both detrimental. Or, as [Rashi] explained there in the Kuntres: "[acting] out of love" [means] out of love of reward — such as where if he will not have a reward he regrets his earlier [deeds], and he only acts in order to receive a reward — and "out of fear" means out of fear of punishment. However, here [in our Gemara] it is difficult, for [the Gemara] treats "out of love" as praiseworthy and "out of fear" as detrimental, whereas it could have said the opposite, or both as detrimental, or both as praiseworthy.

Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:16:1.hebrew: אשר באת לחסות - פירוש: שמיהרת. ותימה, דבפ' "מי שאמר הריני נזיר ושמע חבירו ואמר ואני" (נזיר דף כג: ושם) אומר: רות בת בנו של עגלון, בנו של בלק מלך מואב, היתה; וכשתחשוב שנותיו של אהוד שהרג עגלון עד סוף ימים של אבצן — דהיינו בועז — תמצא יותר ממאתים שנה, ולעת זקנתו נשאה, דכתיב: "לבלתי לכת אחרי הבחורים"! וי"ל: ד"בת בנו של עגלון" לאו דוקא, אלא כלומר דמזרעו היתה, כמו "בן בנו של נמרוד הרשע" (חגיגה דף יג.); ובקרא קרי לה "נערה":
Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:16:1.english: "You have come to take refuge" - Explanation: that you hurried [to come]. And [this is] astonishing! For in the chapter [entitled] Mi she-amar hareini nazir v'shama chaveiro v'amar v'ani (Nazir 23b and there[abouts]), it says: "Ruth was the granddaughter of Eglon, the son of Balak, king of Moab"; and when you calculate the years from Ehud, who killed Eglon, until the end of the days of Ibzan — who is Boaz — you will find [it is] more than two hundred years, and in his old age he married her, as it is written: "not to go after the young men"! And one can answer that "granddaughter of Eglon" is not meant literally; rather, it means that she was from his descendants, like "the grandson of Nimrod the wicked" (Chagigah 13a); and [indeed,] in Scripture it calls her "a young woman."

Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:1:1.hebrew: רבי אליעזר אומר אביה כו' - למיסבר קראי פליגי, אי נמי נפקא מינה אם מתו אביה ואמה או נתגיירו. וריב"ן פירש דלר"ע צריכה שתכפור בעבודת כוכבים קודם שתבעל לו, ולפירושו לא אתי כר"ע הא דקתני לעיל, "בד"א שלא קיבלה עליה":
Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:1:1.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: "Her father," etc. - They disagree [merely] on how to interpret the verses; alternatively, there is a practical difference if her father and mother died or converted. And Rivan explained that according to Rabbi Akiva, she must renounce idolatry before she has relations with him; and according to his explanation, that which was taught above — "When does this apply? When she did not accept [conversion] upon herself" — does not accord with Rabbi Akiva:

Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:3:1.hebrew: ירח שלשים יום - וכן בפ"ק דנזיר (דף ה. ושם): "ואימא שלשים יום, כדכתיב: 'עד חדש ימים'" — משמע דסתם חדש שלשים. והא דאמרי' בר"ה (דף יט:) ובסנהדרין (דף יא. ושם): "כמה עיבור שנה? שלשים יום; רשב"ג אומר: חודש" — היכא דמוכח שאני:
Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:3:1.english: "A month" [is] thirty days - And similarly in the first chapter of Nazir (5a, and there): "And say thirty days, as it is written: 'until a month of days'" — [this] implies that an unspecified "month" [means] thirty [days]. And [as for] that which we say in Rosh Hashanah (19b) and in Sanhedrin (11a, and there): "How long is the intercalation of a year? Thirty days; Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: a month" — where it is evident [from the context that a distinction is intended], it is different.

Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:4:1.hebrew: אין מקיימין - פירש ריב"ן: שלא ינסך יינו. וקשיא לר"י, דא"כ כי אתני בהדיה נמי. ועוד, דמתשובתו של ר' ישמעאל משמע דמדאורייתא פליגי. ונראה לר"י, דטעמא דר' עקיבא לפי שצוה הקב"ה לאברהם למול עבדיו, לכך אסור לקיים שאינם מולין:
Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:4:1.english: One may not maintain - Rivan explained [that the reason is] lest he render his wine nesekh. And this is difficult for the Ri: For if so, when he stipulates with him [that he need not be circumcised, the concern should apply] as well. And furthermore, from Rabbi Yishmael's response it is implied that they disagree on a biblical level. And it appears to the Ri that Rabbi Akiva's reason is because the Holy One, Blessed be He, commanded Abraham to circumcise his slaves; therefore, it is forbidden to maintain [slaves] who are not circumcised.

Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:6:1.hebrew: זה גר תושב - פירש בקונטרס שקבל עליו שלא לעבוד עבודת כוכבים, ומחלל שבת כעובד עבודת כוכבים. וקשה, דאם כן נפישי להו משבע מצות, ובמסכת ע"ז (דף סד:) משמע דבשבע מצות שקבלו בני נח איקרי גר תושב. ועוד, דבפרק ארבע מיתות (סנהדרין דף נח:) אמרי' דעובד כוכבים ששבת חייב מיתה אפילו בחול, כל שכן בשבת. ובפרק ד' מחוסרי כפרה (כריתות דף ט. ושם) קאמר ר"ע דגר תושב אין מוזהר על השבת. ונראה דהכא בעושה מלאכה לצורך ישראל, דומיא ד"וינפש בן אמתך":
Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:6:1.english: This is a ger toshav - Rashi explained that [he is one] who took upon himself not to worship idols, and [that] one who desecrates Shabbat is like an idolater. And this is difficult, because if so, there would be more than seven mitzvot for them, whereas in tractate Avodah Zarah (64b) it is implied that [it is] upon [accepting] the seven mitzvot that the descendants of Noah accepted [that] one is called a ger toshav. And furthermore, in the chapter [entitled] Arba Mitot (Sanhedrin 58b), we say that an idolater who rested [from work] is liable for death even on a weekday, all the more so on Shabbat. And in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Mechusrei Kapparah (Keritot 9a and elsewhere), Rabbi Akiva says that a ger toshav is not commanded regarding Shabbat. And it appears that here [the verse is speaking] of one who performs labor for the needs of a Jew, similar to "that the son of your maidservant may be refreshed" [Exodus 23:12].

Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:8:1.hebrew: היכא דלא פסקא וכו' - פר"ת, דהני מילי אדר' יהושע קאי; ו"לא פסקא למילתיה" היינו שכל שעה דוחה אותו מיום ליום שימול, אבל היכא דפסקא למילתיה שלא ימול כלל — התם אין מקיימין. ולא משמע כן, דה"מ אדר"ע קאי. ונראה לר"י כפירושו, אבל אדר"ע קאי: דהיכא דנתרצה למול ודוחהו — התם אין מקיימין, הואיל ומצוה למול, דשהויי מצוה לא משהינן; אבל היכא דפסק שלא ימול, אינו מחויב למולו בעל כרחו, ומגלגל י"ב חדש עמו, אולי יתרצה. וכן פי' בשערי דרב האי בשער רביעי:
Tosafot on Yevamot 48b:8:1.english: Where he did not make [his refusal] explicit, etc. - Rabbeinu Tam explains that "this applies" refers to Rabbi Yehoshua [ben Levi]: "he did not make his matter explicit" means that he continually puts him off from day to day [saying] that he will be circumcised; but where he made his matter explicit — that he will not be circumcised at all — there "one may not maintain [him]." However, it does not seem so, because "this applies" refers to Rabbi Akiva. And it appears to Ri like his explanation, except that it refers to Rabbi Akiva: where he agreed to be circumcised and puts him off, there "one may not maintain [him]," since it is a mitzvah to circumcise him, for we do not delay a mitzvah; but where he explicitly stated that he will not be circumcised, he is not obligated to circumcise him against his will, and he bears with him for twelve months — perhaps he will agree. And so he explained in Sha'arei of Rav Hai, in the fourth gate.
